(this is a long comment, and I’m sorry to anyone who reads it)

I’m thankful my life turned out better than it could’ve been, it truly could’ve been pretty bad.

I was my birth mom’s fourth kid out of a total of six kids, although I do have one brother on my birth dad’s side. she lived with my birth dad’s parents in their basement when I was first born. My birth dad was sent to life in prison in two separate states right after my birth mom got pregnant with me, so he was never really in the picture, but i did get letters and stuff from him growing up.

My birth mom (& birth dad was too before he went to prison) was a meth addict, so when she was pregnant with me she was on parole and did a lot of meth. After a few positive drug tests they sent her back to jail for the remainder of her pregnancy with me where once I was born, I thankfully came out without withdrawal symptoms.

Because I didn’t have drugs in my system when I was born, I went back home with her. She was still using right after jail/my birth, and my grandparents did as much as they could to help without making a strained addict more pissed off.

whenever my birth mom would get high, or even when she wasn’t using due to withdrawals, she’d hit & scream at me if i cried at all, which would alert my grandparents to try to take me upstairs. That would usually make my birth mom more mad and angry, so my grandparents started to wait until she would go to sleep to take me upstairs for food, baths, etc. I am so so thankful my grandparents were there.

My grandparents said she would take me for days to places they had no idea and they said I would come back smelling something awful. once I hit around a year old, my birth mom decided to start leaving me and doing her own thing. she came to see me less and less and pretty soon it felt like i was only living with my grandparents. I remember her coming back and I would just be terrified of her, and the times I wasn’t terrified she would bring her boyfriends by and i remember feeling so odd about the whole situation.

Once I turned five years old, she was sentenced to prison for five years. I was then adopted by my grandparents. My adopted dad/biological grandfather died when I was eight, which was extremely painful since he retired the year I was born, so we used to spend all of our days together.

Last time I have heard from my bio mom was when I was around 15 years old. I noticed she was out of prison and started to post about me on facebook. oooh that made me so mad because she just abandoned me (which honestly was for the best) but then had the audacity to post me on facebook like she was in my life? I was so upset that she felt the need to pretend I was in her life to her online friends when at the time, the last time I spoke to her was when I was five before she left for prison. I asked her kindly not to post me on facebook, and she told me I was a brat and that she wanted nothing to do with me. honestly I was surprised she used a euphemism like ‘brat’ instead of something harsher since she has in the past. one of my sisters on the other hand apparently took that personally and called me every name in the book. It made no sense. and it hurt, not so much the words themselves but how distant I felt from family. I only had my grandma left, my one nice sister left to live across the country when I was eight, a couple months after my dad (biological grandpa) died. I don’t blame her, but i was lonely. My brother and I didn’t get along amazingly since his mother wasn’t a fan of me or my bio mom being involved with her family.

honestly, I got incredibly lucky to get adopted by my grandparents, they were so kind and caring throughout my entire childhood. My life truly wasn’t bad, just had some tough moments but overall i’m grateful to have the people I do have in my life. Some of these comments have reminded me how lucky I truly got growing up. I’m truly sorry to anyone who has had to experience hatred from a parent, no child (or adult even) should ever have to be put in such a situation.

I didn’t know who my little brothers were for years due to closed adoption rules and just being separated. i finally figured out who they were and we’ve said the occasional “happy birthday!” online, but i don’t want to overstep since one of my brothers is still a minor and the other just became an adult, so I don’t want to overstep any boundaries, especially since I don’t know how much they know or if they even really know who I am. They both got adopted into really good families, and i’m so so happy they had the best childhoods.
